host_pcb_constraints_summary: 100 Ω differential impedance routing for each SATA TX (A+/A-) and RX (B+/B-) pair, length-matched within typical < 5 mil intra-pair skew.
AC-coupling capacitors (typ 10 nF) on each line as required by Serial ATA spec.
ESD protection on the SATA connector pins.
Common-mode choke optional near the connector for EMI mitigation.
Reference-clock distribution to all port PHYs (100 MHz HCSL or 25 MHz crystal + on-die PLL).
DEVSLP sideband: implementation-defined CMOS line — route as a slow-rate digital signal with pull-down on the host PCB.
Activity LED driver (when CAP.SAL=1) — simple open-drain or push-pull to LED + current-limit resistor.

Connector: standard 7-pin SATA signal connector (Gen 1/2/3 use the same pinout); 15-pin SATA power connector separately; eSATA connector for external + cable applications; SATA Express dual-mode connector (SATA + PCIe) for SATA 3.2+ platforms.
Backplane: SES-2 / SGPIO / SAF-TE bus to enclosure processor when CAP.EMS=1.
host_silicon_constraints: Memory-mapped AHCI register block — synthesizable digital RTL; bus interface depends on host (PCI / PCI-X / PCIe).
Per-port DMA engine — system-bus master with credit-based or split-transaction handshake to host memory.
Per-port Command List walker + PRD fetcher + Received FIS poster — purely digital.
Per-port SATA Transport / Link / PHY — hard macro from PHY vendor; integrated through a vendor-defined PIPE-style interface.
Interrupt aggregator — per-port PxIS bits OR'd through PxIE mask into IS.IPS[port], then through GHC.IE to legacy INTx or MSI / MSI-X.
Cache-coherent or IOMMU-aware DMA path is platform / host requirement, not AHCI requirement.
fields.card_internal_constraints: AHCI defines no SATA device-side constraints; the device is a separate IC class with its own datasheet and PHY / firmware / NAND or platter constraints.
fields.notes: AHCI 1.3.1 is a register / protocol / programming-model specification; it does not include normative PDK, SDC, UPF, DRC, or LVS content. PHY characteristic constraints (eye width, jitter budget, return loss, impedance, AC coupling) are normative in Serial ATA 2.6 / 3.x, not in AHCI.
